title: Intent-Aware Self-Correction for Mitigating Social Biases in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the models' reliance on social stereotypes in ambiguous question-answering scenarios involving religious contexts. A non-biased answer is 'unknown' when the context is insufficient, and the measurement evaluates if the model chooses a stereotyped answer instead.
findings: The proposed self-correction methods, particularly cross-model correction with a low-bias feedback model, were found to be effective in reducing stereotypical bias in the religion category. This was demonstrated by significant improvements in accuracy (i.e., choosing the non-biased answer) and reductions in the diff-bias score for all tested language models.
